en.ru:
Оцените своё состояние до и после выполнения упражнений КПТ. Регулярные оценки помогают замечать динамику и понимать, как вы продвигаетесь.

Вы можете выбирать удобный для себя формат. Мы предлагаем два варианта:

Сначала дайте оценку утром. В течение дня выполняйте упражнения, проводите эксперименты или работайте с терапевтом. Вечером повторите оценку, чтобы увидеть изменения.

Или оценивайте самочувствие прямо перед началом работы в приложении или сессией с психологом, а вторую — сразу после завершения упражнений.

Оба способа одинаково полезны. Выберите тот, который подходит вам больше всего.
en.oldText:
Rate how you feel before and after doing CBT exercises. Regular check-ins help you notice changes over time and understand how you’re progressing.

You can choose the format that works best for you. We suggest two options:

First, check in with yourself in the morning. During the day, do your exercises, run behavioral experiments, or work with your therapist. In the evening, rate your state again to see what has changed.

Or you can rate your well-being right before you start working in the app or before a session with your psychologist, and then do a second check-in immediately after you finish the exercises.

Both approaches are equally helpful. Choose the one that feels most natural for you.
en.newText:
Rate how you feel before and after your CBT exercises. Regular check-ins help you notice progress and understand how you’re moving forward.

You can choose the format that works best for you. We suggest two options:

First, do a check-in in the morning. Throughout the day, complete exercises, try new experiments, or work with a psychologist. In the evening, rate how you feel again to see changes.

Or, rate your well-being right before you start working in the app or a session with a psychologist, and then again immediately after you finish your exercises.

Both ways are equally helpful. Choose the one that suits you best.

passes.reason: Translation A is more concise, follows the UX guidelines perfectly, and uses the correct terminology ('psychologist' instead of 'therapist'). Translation B introduces unnecessary complexity and uses 'therapist', which contradicts the glossary.

issues.note: Used 'therapist' instead of the required 'psychologist'
Phrasing like 'check in with yourself' and 'rate your state' is slightly more wordy and less punchy than A's UX-friendly approach
Added 'behavioral' to experiments, which wasn't in the original

passes.reason: Translation A is more idiomatic and flows better as a piece of supportive guidance. It uses natural phrasing like 'notice changes over time' and 'the one that feels most natural for you', whereas B feels slightly more repetitive and mechanical.

issues.note: The phrase 'try new experiments' is a bit clunky compared to the standard CBT term 'run behavioral experiments' or simply 'do experiments'.
The sentence structure in the fourth paragraph is slightly fragmented compared to the smoother flow in A.

en.ru:
Вы уже сделали первую оценку. Теперь попробуйте немного поддержать своё состояние и улучшить самочувствие.

Вы можете воспользоваться инструментами приложения или пройти сессию с психологом — выберите то, что будет для вас комфортно.

Когда завершите, возвращайтесь сюда и ещё раз оцените своё состояние.

Лучше всего сделать повторную оценку в течение дня, чтобы увидеть изменения.
en.oldText:
You’ve already completed your initial check-in. Now try to support yourself a little and gently improve how you’re feeling.

You can use the tools in the app or have a session with your psychologist — choose whatever feels most comfortable for you.

When you’re done, come back here and evaluate your state once again.

It’s best to reassess later in the day to see how things have shifted.
en.newText:
You’ve already completed your first check-in. Now, try to support yourself and improve how you feel.

You can use the tools in the app or have a session with a psychologist — choose whatever feels most comfortable for you.

Once you’re done, come back here and rate how you feel again.

It’s best to re-evaluate your well-being throughout the day to see changes.

passes.reason: Translation A is more natural and follows the UX guidelines perfectly. Translation B uses 'evaluate your state' and 'reassess', which sound overly clinical and heavy compared to the warm, supportive tone required.

issues.note: 'evaluate your state' and 'reassess' are too formal/clinical; 'how you feel' or 'rate your mood' is better for a supportive tone.
'your psychologist' implies the user already has one, whereas the original 'с психологом' is more general.
'how things have shifted' is a bit wordy compared to the direct 'see changes'.

passes.reason: Translation A sounds more natural and empathetic, using 'how you're feeling' and 'how things have shifted' which fits the 'understanding friend' tone. Translation B is slightly more clinical and repetitive.

issues.note: The phrase 'rate how you feel again' is a bit clunky compared to 'evaluate your state once again' or 'reassess'.
The phrase 'throughout the day' changes the nuance of 'в течение дня' (within the day/later in the day) to imply a continuous process, whereas the original suggests a single follow-up point.

passes.reason: Translation A correctly follows the 'sentence case' rule for UI elements as specified in the instructions, whereas Translation B uses Title Case, which is incorrect for this context.

issues.note: Uses Title Case instead of sentence case for a UI label

passes.reason: The original is a title/header. According to the style guide, titles can use Title Case, and 'Daily Well-Being Check-In' looks more professional and polished for a header than sentence case.

issues.note: Uses sentence case for a title, which is less common for main headers in this context compared to Title Case.

en.ru:
Этот показатель отражает, насколько продуктивно вы поработали в приложении — он учитывает несколько важных параметров.

Чем выше итоговый результат, тем увереннее и быстрее вы продвигаетесь к улучшению своего психологического самочувствия.
en.oldText:
This metric reflects how productively you used the app — it takes several key factors into account.

The higher your final score, the more confidently and quickly you move toward better psychological well-being.
en.newText:
This score reflects how productively you’ve worked in the app — it takes several important parameters into account.

The higher your score, the more confidently and quickly you’re moving toward improving your mental well-being.

the phrasing 'how productively you used the app' is slightly less natural than 'how productively you've worked in the app' in this context
